Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

polymer 0.3.0

polymer is rebuilt on ‘wkpool’ and ‘cdtr’. This release breaks the old interface.

  • polymer is now MIT licensed (was GPL-3), matching ‘cdtr’ and ‘wk’, so the overlay core can be reused freely.

  • New vignette “Identity and n-ary overlay with polymer” works through r-spatial/sf#1959 (Esri Identity) and r-spatial/sf#2242 (n-ary intersection of one layer), shows Intersect, Union, Identity, Erase and Symmetrical Difference as filters on one mesh, and sets out where ‘sf’ prepares the inputs and where the workflow stays on polymer’s own tables.

  • New article “Overlay robustness: the history of issue 7” records issue 7 from 2020 to 2026, reruns its examples against GEOS 3.12.1 and 3.15.0, and documents where polymer itself still fails.

  • polymer() takes any number of layers as anything ‘wk’ can read, not only ‘sf’ data frames. Vertices are shared on exact coordinate equality with ‘wkpool’, and all edges are triangulated once with ‘cdtr’, which inserts crossings as new vertices.

  • Triangles are now labelled per feature rather than per ring, so holes are subtracted instead of being counted as an extra overlap.

  • The polymer object holds mesh (a ‘wkpool’ triangle pool), index (triangle, layer, feature), layers (attributes of each input) and crs. The old input, primitives and geometry_map elements are gone.

  • New fuse() dissolves the mesh into overlay pieces, one per distinct set of covering features, as an exact partition with shared vertices.

  • layer_n() now returns the dissolved pieces covered at least n times, with geometry as wk::wkb(), instead of one ‘sf’ polygon per triangle.

  • ‘RTriangle’ (non-commercial licence), ‘silicate’, ‘gibble’, ‘sf’ and the tidyverse packages are no longer dependencies; ‘sf’ is in Suggests. The %>% re-export is removed.

  • The soil and field data now carry a current ‘sf’ crs object.

  • Now use wk and geos for input handling, and output of layer_n().

Developed by Michael Sumner.
